questions.stem: In post-coordinate indexing, who combines the concepts of a subject?

options.A: The searcher or the retrieval system, at the moment of searching
options.B: The indexer, at the moment the document is indexed
options.C: The cataloguer, before the document is shelved
options.D: The author, before the document is published

questions.explanation: In post-coordinate indexing concepts are assigned separately as individual terms, and it is the searcher or the retrieval system that combines them together at the moment of searching.

questions.stem: Which statement gives two correct differences between pre-coordinate and post-coordinate indexing?

options.A: Pre-coordinate combines concepts while the document is being indexed; post-coordinate leaves each term separately searchable for combination later, during retrieval
options.B: Pre-coordinate combines concepts during retrieval; post-coordinate combines them before indexing
options.C: Both systems combine concepts only at the point of searching
options.D: Pre-coordinate leaves each term separately searchable; post-coordinate combines them in advance

questions.explanation: The essential difference is timing: pre-coordinate indexing combines concepts while the document is being indexed, whereas post-coordinate indexing leaves each term separately searchable and lets the combination happen later, during retrieval.

options.A: An early post-coordinate approach that assigns individual, single terms to documents and combines them only at the point of retrieval
options.B: A pre-coordinate method that derives entries from a classification chain
options.C: A classified display that groups terms alphabetically from A to Z
options.D: A syntactic system that uses role operators to preserve context

questions.explanation: Uniterm indexing is an early and influential example of the post-coordinate approach: individual, single terms are assigned to documents and combined only at the point of retrieval.

questions.stem: Why can post-coordinate searching produce high recall but low precision if handled poorly?

options.A: Results can be affected by inconsistent or uncontrolled terminology, and a poorly formed search can retrieve many irrelevant documents
options.B: Because the indexer must anticipate every useful combination in advance
options.C: Because free-text searching never matches synonyms of a word
options.D: Because optical coincidence cards cannot be combined electronically

questions.explanation: Post-coordinate flexibility comes at a cost: results can be affected by inconsistent or uncontrolled terminology, and a poorly formed search can produce high recall but low precision.

questions.stem: Which problem can free-text searching suffer from?

options.A: Synonyms not being matched, ambiguous words, and variations in spelling
options.B: The requirement that every document receive a controlled vocabulary term
options.C: The impossibility of combining two or three terms with AND
options.D: The loss of all access points except the leading term

questions.explanation: Free-text searching looks directly in titles, abstracts or full text without relying entirely on a controlled vocabulary, so it can suffer from synonyms not being matched, ambiguous words, and variations in spelling.
